title: Costs rebuild 2 · piece 3: measure records vs snapshots on live data (gate for the read switch)
description:
**Piece 3 of LIN-4195.** This piece is a measurement and a gate, not a feature. It needs piece 2 to have run live long enough for lineages to hold both records and snapshots.

**Measure, on live data, for lineages holding both records and snapshots:**

* **To the cent (review note 5):** restrict to lineages that meet all of these:
  * the snapshot is priced;
  * there are no subagents;
  * there is one model;
  * the last record is at or before the last snapshot.

  For these, the records sum must equal the snapshot-derived figure to the cent. A disagreement blocks piece 4 until it is explained.
* For lineages with records after their last snapshot, expect `records ≥ snapshot`. Report the excess as the L4/L5 tail recovery.
* Report the share of runner work that Harbour can price today (snapshot-only), and what it would be from records.
* Report the share of lineages that are record-backed vs snapshot-only.
* Report counts of lineages whose records look like a subset of their snapshots. This is the D7 residue (a pre-deploy transcript that was unreachable at first post).
* Report rejected and skipped counts from the runner oplog.
* **Volume (D13):**
  * record counts per lineage and per window;
  * `explain` on the `listForAnchors` query with the declared index;
  * a timed `/kpis` and workspace-KPIs read against live-sized record volume.

  If either is too slow, record that the D13 fallback (pre-summing records of models without a tier override) is needed in piece 4.

**Output:** a comment on LIN-4195 with the numbers and the query or script used, so the measurement can be repeated in piece 6. Any one-off script goes under `scripts/` with a header that says what it measures.

**Acceptance:**

* The comparison is reported.
* The to-the-cent subset agrees, or each disagreement is explained.
* A go / no-go call for piece 4 is stated, with its reason.

---

**Parent:** LIN-4195 "Costs rebuild 2: one record per model request, summed". Its full design (decisions D1–D14, the replay change list, the witnesses, the order of landing) is in LIN-4195's description under "## Implementation Plan". The plan-review notes are in LIN-4195's comment `eedab867-0fe0-4b15-b74a-2b78240f11d1`. The numbered notes cited here ("review note N") refer to that comment.

Session fit: fits one session
Plan-review due: no — covered by LIN-4195's approving plan-review (comment eedab867-0fe0-4b15-b74a-2b78240f11d1, rev 1)
Grounding commits: Harbour (JKershaw/LinearViewer) `72305215`, runner (JKershaw/simple-dispatcher) `cc2650a`. At breakdown (2026-11-04 \~01:45Z) neither repo had a commit after these.

The parent's approved plan is this piece's starting point; read it in full in LIN-4195's description. Follow it. Where the code shows it is wrong, change course and say so on LIN-4195.

## Implemented (close-out)

Implemented as scoped, with no plan sections to prune (this description holds only the problem statement, acceptance and scope, which are kept). PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2267](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2267>), merged as `230cc2c2`: two read-only scripts under `scripts/` (`lin-4200-measure-records-vs-snapshots.mjs`, `lin-4200-d13-volume-timing.mjs`), their fixture tests and a census allowlist entry. Deviation: the to-the-cent rule was amended by ruling `lin4200-to-cent-rule`, and coverage is judged by post time (`updatedAt`). Result and the NO-GO for piece 4: LIN-4195 comment `0beba2a2-4378-4ee6-a46a-d5f1291b59ec`. Full history is in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

### LIN-4200 · beat 1 (ground and set up): BLOCKED on live data access

**Set up**
- LIN-4200 set to In Progress.
- Branch `feat/lin-4200-measure-records-vs-snapshots` created in the Harbour clone (from main `9cc5ff9c`). No commits yet.
- Staleness since the breakdown (01:42Z): Harbour changed only in LIN-4197 (`1b6c6758`, fixtures) and LIN-4198 (`9cc5ff9c`: store, intake, `priceRequest`, the `{urlKey, rootItemId}` index, routes). The read itself is unchanged and still snapshot-only: `lib/cost-read.js`, `lib/row-usage.js`, `lib/kpi-stats.js`, `lib/workspace-kpi-stats.js`. Runner changed in LIN-4197 (`b6fc9ab`) and LIN-4199 (`9478e1c`, records posted for claude-code, snapshots still posted).
- Two corrections for piece 3 (from LIN-4195 comments): subagent files also sit under `<session-id>/subagents/workflows/wf_*/agent-*.jsonl` (e5b942fb); and a message id present in both the main and a subagent file must be counted once (5afcf3e3 (a)).

**Data access: no route to live Harbour rows from this machine**
- Live `request-usage` and dispatch rows are in the production Mongo behind harbour.cat. There is no `MONGODB_URI` or Harbour `.env` here, and no read endpoint for `request-usage` records. `/issues/{id}/cost` is snapshot-based and aggregated per issue. Snapshot `[usage]` feedback is visible per item via `GET /dispatch/{id}`, but that is per item, not a bulk read.
- The local mongod at 127.0.0.1:27017 (`linear-viewer` db) is NOT live data: 0 dispatch-history, 0 dispatch-queue, 0 request-usage, 0 llm-call-log docs. I did not use it.
- Readable here: the runner's live state. `/Users/autopilot/development/simple-dispatcher/state/oplog.jsonl` (103,713 lines), and the dispatcher (pid 65238, started 04:59:29Z, after the LIN-4199 merge) is posting records. Its first `request-usage.flush` (05:00:09Z, reason=stop) reports posted=136, failed=0; 19 flush events so far.

**Blocker, and what would unblock it**
1. A read-only Mongo connection to the production `linear-viewer` db (or a Harbour-host run of the measurement script), plus the workspace `urlKey`.
2. Time. Records only exist since about 05:00Z today. The gate needs piece 2 to run long enough for lineages to hold both records and snapshots. Today's sample would be a handful of lineages. No go/no-go is possible yet, and I am not treating piece 4 as a go.

**Measurement design (grounded in the code; to run in beat 3)**
- **Lineage**: dispatch rows (queue ∪ history) grouped by `anchorOf(row)` = `rootItemId || _id` (`lib/lineage-membership.js`). Records join on the `rootItemId` the intake takes from the taken row (`lib/request-usage-intake.js`). Count orphans: records whose anchor no longer matches a row's current anchor, after a re-point (`lib/dispatch-store.js` ~L321).
- **Record figure**: tokens = sum of the five fields over the lineage's `request-usage` docs (`listForAnchors` projection). Cost = sum of `priceRequest(record)`, claude-code has `costUsd: null`, so each record is priced at its own prompt size.
- **Snapshot figure**: `foldLineageUsage` over the lineage's rows, each row's last `kind:'usage'` entry (`lib/row-usage.js`, `lib/session-telemetry.js`). Tokens and cost come from that same fold.
- **Priced by snapshot**: the snapshot fold's `completeness === 'complete'`. This is the running-total guard too: a Haiku snapshot over the 100k threshold is `unpriced`.
- **Subagents**: any record with `agent !== 'main'`. A snapshot never includes subagent spend (`walkUsage` reads the main transcript only). For a snapshot-only lineage, check the runner-host transcript dirs (both subagent layouts) if the transcript still exists; otherwise report "unknown".
- **One model**: distinct `resolveWorkerModelId(record.model)` over the records, excluding `<synthetic>`, has size 1 and equals the snapshot's `model`.
- **Last record / last snapshot**: last record = max `at` over the lineage's records. `at` is the first transcript line's timestamp for that message id, set once on insert. Last snapshot = the `timestamp` of the lineage's last `kind:'usage'` feedback entry. The snapshot has no covered-through field, so its post time is the cover point.
- **To-the-cent subset**: priced snapshot AND no subagents AND one model AND last record ≤ last snapshot. Agreement needs both: (a) all five integer token sums equal, and (b) the cost difference is under half a cent. Token equality is the stricter test and separates coverage from pricing, because flat-rate cost is linear in tokens.
- **Explained differences** (each from the code, so a disagreement is either one of these or a blocker):
  (i) id-less transcript lines: `walkUsage` counts each as its own message (`line:${i}`); records skip them and count `skipped.noRequestId`;
  (ii) `<synthetic>` messages: `walkUsage` includes their tokens and can make its last-seen model `<synthetic>`; records skip them;
  (iii) a message id in both main and subagent files: one request on both sides, counted once with the first-seen agent;
  (iv) timing: records posted after the snapshot's walk (the L4 tail).
- **L4/L5 tail**: lineages with last record > last snapshot. Expect records ≥ snapshot on every token field. Report the excess per field and in dollars (priced separately, not subtracted).
- **D7 residue**: lineages with both where the record token sum is below the snapshot's on any of the five fields. Report the count and the dollar gap.
- **Record-backed vs snapshot-only**: a lineage with ≥1 record is record-backed. Otherwise it is snapshot-only. No usage at all is reported separately.
- **Share of runner work priced**: tokens (five fields summed) in lineages the legacy read prices, over all runner tokens. The same share from records (record tokens whose `priceRequest` is non-null, over all record tokens). Both token-weighted and by lineage count.
- **Oplog counters**: sum `rejected` and `skipped.noRequestId` over `request-usage.flush` events; count `request-usage.error` and each `skip` value (`no-transcript`, `no-token`, `no-item`). Only events after 05:00Z are records-era. Cross-check `rejected` against the Harbour-side `rejected`.
- **D13 volume**: request-usage docs per lineage and per 13-day window. `explain('executionStats')` on `find({urlKey, rootItemId: {$in}}, LIST_PROJECTION)`, using the declared `{urlKey, rootItemId}` index (`lib/db-indexes.js`). Time `/kpis` and workspace-KPIs on live-sized volume. If either is too slow, record that the D13 pre-summing fallback is needed in piece 4.
- **Repeatability**: the script goes at `scripts/lin-4200-measure-records-vs-snapshots.mjs`, with a header saying what it measures. Not written yet; it waits for access.

**Go/no-go for piece 4**: not decided. Pending live access and enough days of records.

### LIN-4200 · beat 2 status: script and fixtures done, live run BLOCKED on Railway SSH access

**Done (local commit `23326722` on `feat/lin-4200-measure-records-vs-snapshots`, not pushed)**
- `scripts/lin-4200-measure-records-vs-snapshots.mjs`: read-only (find() only). It classifies each lineage with the production fold (`lineageRecords`, `foldLineageUsage`, `lineageFigure`, `priceRequest`, `resolveWorkerModelId`). It reports the to-the-cent subset, the L4/L5 tail, D7 residue, shares, record-backed vs snapshot-only, orphan records, the oplog counters and UNMEASURED case classes.
- `tests/unit/lin-4200-measure.test.js`: 17 fixture tests, all passing (`node --test tests/unit/lin-4200-measure.test.js`). Mutation check: removing the subagent exclusion from the to-the-cent rule fails the subagent test (1 fail, observed), and restoring it returns 17/17.

**Blocked: live read**
- Railway CLI is logged in and the Harbour project resolves. The `MongoDB-harbour` service has no public TCP proxy, and `railway connect --ssh` needs an SSH key registered with Railway. This machine has none (`railway ssh keys add` would register one on the account). Nothing has been registered.
- So no live measurement has run yet. Window and counts are pending.

Generate an ed25519 key and register it via railway ssh keys add

### LIN-4200 · beat 2 result: live measurement run (read-only), gate NOT passed as written

**Window.** Harbour request-usage, workspace `linearviewer`: 2069 records, first first-line time 2026-11-03T19:28:39.924Z (pre-deploy, posted after the LIN-4199 deploy), last 2026-11-04T07:46:16.501Z. Runner oplog counted from 2026-11-04T04:59:21Z.

**To-the-cent subset** (priced snapshot, no subagents, one model, last record <= last snapshot): 20 eligible.
- 1 agrees exactly (88f03588, snapshot lags its last record by 6.3 s).
- 19 disagree by exactly ONE final request. In each, that request's first transcript line leads the last snapshot by 353-460 ms; the snapshot walk raced the line reaching disk (same-Stop race). Records exceed the snapshot in every token field by that one request. Each is classified sameStopRace; 0 unexplained.
- The race window (2 s) was chosen after the first live run, not fixed in advance; disclosed.
- Consequence: the rule "last record <= last snapshot implies the snapshot covers it" is false at Stop time, so the to-the-cent gate cannot pass as written. No pricing or record-side error was found.

**Tail (records after last snapshot):** 0 in this sample. The reap/cancel tail path (L4/L5 recovery) is UNMEASURED: no reap-only lineage was in the sample.

**D7 residue:** 0 lineages with records below their snapshot.

**Shares** (token-weighted over 394.4M snapshot tokens / 405.7M record tokens): snapshot prices 97.3% of tokens (383.7M). The one lineage it cannot price is 3ccfa072 (this ticket's chain: Haiku over 100k, snapshot null, records price it). Records price 100%. By lineage: snapshot-priced 27/28 (96.4%); record-priced 28/28.

**Lineages:** 28 with usage, all 28 record-backed, 0 snapshot-only, 2 no-usage.

**Oplog** (runner, from 04:59:21Z): 136 flush events; posted 2069; rejected 0; failed 0; deferred 0; skipped.noRequestId 0; request-usage.error 0; skip reasons none.

**Case classes in the sample:** present: subagents (1 lineage, excluded from the subset), mixed-model (6 lineages), Haiku over 100k (1), resumed across deploy (pre-deploy records present). UNMEASURED: one-turn lineage, <synthetic> tail, killed/reaped with no Stop, reap-flush tail.

**Commands:** derived MONGODB_URI via Railway at run time, then node scripts/lin-4200-measure-records-vs-snapshots.mjs --out <scratchpad>/measure-live-3.json. Tests: node --test tests/unit/lin-4200-measure.test.js (21 pass); npm run test:unit (22,880 pass, 0 fail, after the census allowlist update).

**Recommendation (for the gate owner, not decided here):** do not treat piece 4 as a go on this rule. Amend to-the-cent to exclude the same-Stop race class (explicitly named, 2 s window), then re-measure after more days, including the reap-flush tail and more subagent/resumed lineages.

### LIN-4200 · beat 3 result: D13 volume and timing (read-only against production)

**Volume (live):** 2,319 request records over 34 lineages. Per lineage: min 15, median 36, p95 211, max 295. Per UTC day: 2026-11-03 243, 2026-11-04 2,076 (to 07:54Z). Since the 04:59:21Z deploy: 935 records, which is 320 per hour. That is about 7,700 a day, consistent with the review's ~100k per 13 days.

**explain('executionStats') on the listForAnchors query** (find {urlKey, rootItemId: {$in}} with LIST_PROJECTION). Every case uses IXSCAN on urlKey_1_rootItemId_1, with no COLLSCAN, and keysExamined = docsExamined = nReturned:
- one task (1 anchor): nReturned 128, 1 ms
- 30-day /kpis window (3,969 dispatch anchors): nReturned 2,319, 6 ms
- record lineages (34 anchors): nReturned 2,319, 4 ms
- scratch at 230,745 records (1,846 anchors): nReturned 230,745, 242 ms

**Timings** (5 repetitions each, median):
- Production, today's /kpis (collectKpiStats): 1,079 ms (range 972-1,203)
- Production, workspace KPIs (collectWorkspaceKpis): 828 ms (804-958)
- Production, records-sum path, 30-day window (2,319 records): 86 ms (81-90)
- Production, records-sum path, one task: 36 ms
- Scratch copy on a local mongod (no tunnel), records-sum path: 5k records 26 ms; 50k 249 ms; 200k 1,048 ms; steady 230,745 records 1,177 ms (1,144-1,209). Fit: about 5.3 us per record, and it predicts the steady measurement within 3%.

**Projection basis:** 320 records per hour since deploy, scaled to 30 days = 230,745 records. The rate is measured over 2.9 h after deploy, so it includes some backlog from pre-deploy transcripts. It matches the review's 100k-per-13-days rate.

**Caveats:** production timings go through an SSH tunnel from one laptop, so they are upper bounds for in-cluster latency. The steady projection is timed on a local mongod, not Railway hardware. Per-record cost is mostly Node-side. The pre-summing fallback itself has not been timed.

**Verdict** (thresholds are my judgment): a page read that is not cached should stay within 1 s at steady state. Piece 4 may add at most 0.5 s to such a read.
- /kpis is not too slow. It is stale-while-revalidate (lib/kpi-page.js, 60 s), so only the background refresh pays the cost. At steady state that refresh is about 2.3 s. The D13 fallback is not needed here.
- Workspace KPIs is too slow if the records-sum path runs on every load. Today it is 0.83 s. Adding about 1.2 s at steady state gives roughly 2 s per page load, above both thresholds. Piece 4 needs either the D13 fallback (pre-summing non-override models in the database, untimed here) or the same cache that /kpis uses. Caching is cheaper and needs no fallback, so I would try it first.

**Commands:** the production URI is derived through the forward at run time. Then: scripts/lin-4200-d13-volume-timing.mjs --scale-local --out <scratchpad>/d13-run1.json, with MONGODB_SCRATCH_URI=mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017. Tests: node --test tests/unit/lin-4200-d13.test.js (11 pass). npm run test:unit: 22,891 pass, 0 fail. Commit 49133a53 (local).

Exclude the same-Stop race class from to-the-cent, then re-measure

### LIN-4200 summary: PR, CI, and LIN-4195 comments (status: In Progress, left open for review)

- **PR:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2267 (open, not merged)
- **Head SHA:** `c5c390bfa5df3ae70242a08af9336a21f68e01b0`
- **CI:** run https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/actions/runs/41797321425 is **success** on the head. Checks: Secret scan (source), Unit tests, E2E shards 1 to 4, and the aggregate `CI success`, all green. The earlier head `ea4c00a7` (run https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/actions/runs/41796374807) was also fully green.
- **LIN-4195 comments:**
  - `fad28679-6c0d-4a11-a10a-f67f3874a21b`: the piece 3 report, with the NO-GO on the rule as written and the statement that "last record <= last snapshot implies coverage" is false at Stop.
  - `e42259ad-056c-4e9c-8b46-2cb6ceda4de0`: the follow-up, with ruling `lin4200-to-cent-rule` applied, the re-measured numbers, and GO with conditions for piece 4.

## Review — LIN-4200

Reviewed PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2267 at head `c5c390bfa5df3ae70242a08af9336a21f68e01b0` (4 commits on main `5334c81a`; mergeable). The scope matches the plan: two read-only scripts under `scripts/` with headers, two fixture test files, and a census allowlist entry. No production code changed. Staleness: no commits to `lib/cost-read.js`, `row-usage.js`, `model-pricing.js`, `request-usage-store.js`, `db-indexes.js`, `kpi-stats.js` or `workspace-kpi-stats.js` since the ticket was created, other than LIN-4198 `9cc5ff9c`, which the work already grounds on. Regression check: the only existing file touched, `tests/unit/lin-4198-request-usage-store.test.js`, has one prior commit (9cc5ff9c). The change only widens the allowlist, with a reason given for each entry.

CI: green on head c5c390bf (run 41797321425: Unit tests, E2E 1–4, Secret scan, `CI success`). I also ran `node --test tests/unit/lin-4200-measure.test.js tests/unit/lin-4200-d13.test.js` locally: 32 pass, 0 fail.

### Main finding: the "reap-flush tail UNMEASURED" claim is false, and the tail is probably filed under the race class

Both LIN-4195 reports say the tail had 0 records after the last snapshot and that the reap-flush tail is UNMEASURED ("no reap-only lineage in the sample"). Condition 2 of the GO rests on that claim. The runner oplog (`simple-dispatcher/state/oplog.jsonl`, from 04:59:21Z) says otherwise:
- There are **34 `request-usage.flush` events with `reason:"reap"`**, and each posted exactly 1 record. They span 32 of 50 sessions.
- The usual pattern: a stop flush posts N records, a second stop flush posts 1 record 3–9 s later, and a reap flush posts 1 more. Example: session e73cde05: stop 32 at 05:02:00.6, stop 1 at 05:02:04.4, reap 1 at 05:02:07.6. By the 08:06 run there were 33 race-class lineages and about 30 reap flushes, each posting 1 record.
- Why the script sees no tail: `recordsAfterSnapshot` and `lastRecordBeforeSnapshot` both key on `record.at`. That is the first transcript line's time, not when the record was posted. A final request that is written just before the Stop walk, but posted by the trailing stop flush or the reap flush after the snapshot, is classed as "at or before the snapshot". It then lands in the to-the-cent set and is relabelled `sameStopRace`. The store keeps the post time as `updatedAt` (`$max`, `lib/request-usage-store.js`), and the script's `find` already returns that field. It just never reads it.
- So the evidence points to one population under two names. The race class (33 lineages) is very likely the L4/L5 tail recovery that the ticket asks to report as excess, in tokens and dollars. The reported tail (0 lineages, $0 excess) and the UNMEASURED reap tail are then wrong. I could not confirm the join from here: I have no production access and did not use the operator's credentials. But the oplog shape and the "gap is exactly the last record" result both point this way.
- Effect on the gate: an unexplained disagreement still looks unlikely, so GO on the amended rule may well stand. But the reported tail, the dollar excess and condition 2 have to be re-derived. The ruling (`lin4200-to-cent-rule`) is not reopened by this; whether its 2 s window is even needed falls out of the fix.

**Fix (implementation):** in `scripts/lin-4200-measure-records-vs-snapshots.mjs`:
1. Compute `lastPostedMs = max(updatedAt)`, and classify `recordsAfterSnapshot` by post time (`updatedAt > snapshotAt`), not by first-line `at`.
2. For each `sameStopRace` member, record whether its last record's `updatedAt` is after the snapshot. Report how many race-class members are late posts and how many are true same-walk races.
3. Report the tail excess per field and in dollars for those lineages.
4. Cross-check against the oplog by `sessionId`: count trailing-stop and reap flushes that posted after the session's first stop flush.
5. Add a fixture test where `at` ≤ snapshot < `updatedAt` and confirm it lands in the tail. Mutation-check it.

Then re-run read-only. Post a corrected follow-up on LIN-4195 (leave the earlier ones unedited) that replaces "reap-flush tail UNMEASURED" and "tail 0" with the measured figures, and restates condition 2.

### Test quality (mutation checks; all reverted, tree clean)
- Removing `gapIsLastRecord` from the race test: 1 fail. Good.
- `toCentSubset = toCent` (exclusion removed): 1 fail. Good.
- Dropping `lastRecordBeforeSnapshot`: 1 fail. Good.
- Dropping `snapshotPriced` from eligibility: 1 fail. Good.
- Dropping the `<synthetic>` model exclusion: 1 fail. Good.
- `agrees = tokensEqual` (cent comparison removed): **21/21 pass, so nothing pins the cent check.** Tiered pricing means equal tokens can still give a different cost, so this is the "to the cent" half of the rule. **Fix:** add a fixture with equal tokens and a different `fold.costUsd` (or records over the long-context tier). It must come out as `agrees === false`.
- Dropping `lagMs >= 0`: stays green. That condition is already implied by `lastRecordBeforeSnapshot`, so this is not a defect. Close-out may delete it.

### Other findings (minor)
- `scripts/lin-4200-d13-volume-timing.mjs`: the scratch guard only checks that the host is `127.0.0.1` or `localhost`. Production itself was reached through a loopback SSH forward, so a mistyped `MONGODB_SCRATCH_URI` could point the `dropDatabase`/`insertMany` scratch path at production. The damage is limited to new `lin4200_d13_scratch_*` names, but the guard does not do what its comment says. **Fix:** also refuse when the scratch URI's host:port equals `MONGODB_URI`'s, and refuse any port other than the one passed in `--scratch-port` (default 27017).
- The D13 script uses `urlKey = distinct('urlKey')[0]`. That is arbitrary when more than one workspace has records. Accept `--url-key`, as the measure script does.
- `historyAnchors` reads only `dispatch-history`, not `dispatch-queue`. The 30-day anchor set slightly undercounts live rows. It does not matter at today's volume.
- The read-only constraint is met by the code (find, distinct, aggregate and explain only; the KPI collectors it calls write nothing). The run, though, used the Mongo root credential, not a read-only one. LIN-4205 (rotation) covers that.

### Isolated, or one of a class?
The class here is "coverage judged by first-line `at` instead of post time". In this PR it shows up in two places in the measure script: tail classification and to-the-cent eligibility. Both are inside, and both are covered by the fix above. Piece 4 (LIN-4201) will sum records regardless of `at`, so the read itself is not affected. No other instance in this PR.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside** (bounded: "records after last snapshot → report excess as L4/L5 tail"; the GO's condition 2 depends on it): the tail and reap-flush figures in the LIN-4195 reports. CI runs only fixtures. Settle **before merge** with the re-run above. The distinguishing condition is a lineage whose last record has `at ≤ snapshotAt < updatedAt`. Such lineages must appear as tail with records ≥ snapshot per field, not as `sameStopRace`.
- **Inside** (the to-the-cent rule): the cent-comparison branch. No test fails when it is removed. Settle **before merge** with the added fixture, mutation-checked.
- **Inside**: every live number (window, shares, oplog counters, D13 timings). These are production reads that CI cannot reach. Settle **before merge** with the corrected re-run's output posted on LIN-4195. The D13 numbers do not need a re-run.
- **Inside** (a GO condition): workspace-KPIs caching or the D13 fallback before the read switch. This is a precondition for piece 4, not work for this PR. Settle **after the deploy** by having close-out confirm the condition is written into LIN-4201's acceptance. That does not settle the measurement itself.
- **Outside**: the Mongo root password exposed in a transcript is LIN-4205 (already filed). The Railway SSH key `lin4200-measurement` and its local key file should be removed. That is not filed, and close-out should file it (check first that it does not already exist).

### Verdict
Request Changes. The gate report misclassifies late-posted final records (34 reap flushes and the trailing stop flushes, visible in the runner oplog) as the same-Stop race. The tail and dollar excess the ticket asks for are therefore reported as 0, and the GO's "reap tail UNMEASURED" condition is false. Next action: **implementation** on LIN-4200 (the script fix and the cent fixture above, a read-only re-run, and a corrected LIN-4195 follow-up). Then review re-runs.

### Reply to review a4e7534a (PR #2267, head `4ab64a1b`)

### The orphan anchors: the cause is in the intake, not the script
On the autopilot note: all three orphan anchors are **`kind:'wake'` rows of autopilot `88f03588`** (LIN-4196):
- `89729833`: taken 08:10:49
- `2e2844c3`: taken 08:11:05
- `df89daf5`: taken 08:11:21

All three were completed together at 08:11:34.622. Their three records were posted between 08:10:46 and 08:11:18, while each wake was running.

The code explains it:
- `addItem` gives a wake row `rootItemId = its own _id`. It skips the factory's inheritance.
- `addFeedback` then latches the producer's `rootItemId` onto the doc on the first tagged feedback (`update.$set = { rootItemId }`, `lib/dispatch-store.js` ~L3270). `runOf` (~L320) documents this exact caveat: a wake row's doc `rootItemId` "is never trusted for a wake".
- The usage intake ignores that caveat. `readTakenForUsage` and `anchorOf(row)` (`lib/request-usage-intake.js` L166) stamp each record with the anchor the row has **at post time**.

So a wake that posts usage before its first tagged feedback leaves its records under its own id. Once the row is re-pointed to the lineage root, no member row carries that anchor. That matches the script's report: `readWorkspace` fetches rows by `_id ∈ recordAnchors`, so the wake rows were read, and they grouped under the re-pointed anchor.

This is not a gap in the script's anchor set. It is a real attribution defect in the piece-1 intake (LIN-4198, Done). Piece 4's `listForAnchors` would drop these records. The NO-GO's reason 1 stands, and its cause is now identified. Its fix belongs to LIN-4195, not to this measurement PR.

**Class:** any record posted while its row's doc `rootItemId` still differs from the value it is later latched to. Wake rows are the known instance. A fix at the intake (resolve a wake through `followUpTo`, as `runOf` does), or re-keying records on the latch, covers the whole class.
